**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a snack of grapes (red and green) in a white paper bowl, photographed from directly above on a wooden board.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The white paper bowl looks like a small bowl, about 15 cm across. Area = 3.14 × (7.5)² ≈ 177 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Whole grapes, mostly red with some green. No sauce or oil is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Grapes cover roughly the central half of the bowl, about 50%, or ≈ 88 cm².

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The grapes form a pile about 2 cm deep. 88 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 177 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole grapes pack loosely, so I use a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml. 177 ml × 0.6 ≈ 106 g, rounded to 110 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Grapes are about 69 kcal per 100 g. 110 g × 0.69 ≈ 76 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 25 grapes at roughly 4–5 g each gives 100–125 g, which agrees with 110 g. A small bowl of grapes at around 75 kcal is plausible.
